meta.description: Tests gene lists, ranked vectors, and fold-change vectors against KEGG pathways and modules with clusterProfiler enrichKEGG/enrichMKEGG (ORA), gseKEGG (GSEA), and SPIA/graphite (signed-topology perturbation) in R. Covers why a KEGG result is a timestamped join against a live REST API, why enrichKEGG keyType is kegg/ncbi-geneid not OrgDb ENSEMBL/SYMBOL, why organism is a KEGG code with prokaryotic locus tags, and why SPIA works only on signaling maps.
meta.environment: R 4.4.3 / Bioconductor 3.20 (F:\OpenScience\audit-envs\crispr-screen-analyst); clusterProfiler 4.14.6, org.Hs.eg.db 3.20.0, gson 0.2.1, SPIA 2.58.0, graphite 1.52.0, pathview 1.46.0, KEGGREST 1.46.0 -- one Bioconductor cycle behind the frontmatter's claimed clusterProfiler 4.18+/graphite 1.56+/SPIA 2.50+ (SPIA itself is at or above). All data are freshly generated SYNTHETIC inputs planted with real KEGG pathway gene membership fetched live from rest.kegg.jp: human genes from hsa04110 (Cell cycle, planted UP) and hsa04910 (Insulin signaling pathway, planted DOWN) against a 3000-gene random background from org.Hs.eg.db; E. coli locus tags from eco00010 (Glycolysis) against a background assembled from other eco metabolic pathways.
meta.regression_note: First audit of this Skill; no prior report exists.

scientific_integrity.detail: 8 references in SKILL.md are real, correctly attributed papers (Kanehisa & Goto 2000, Kanehisa et al. 2023, Wu et al. 2021, Tarca et al. 2009, Draghici et al. 2007, Sales et al. 2012, Luo & Brouwer 2013, Khatri et al. 2012) -- all well-known, verifiable citations in this literature. No DOI/PMID, p-value, sample size, or effect size is invented anywhere in the Skill or in any of my 7 runs; every number in this report came from a run recorded under run/.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure functional-genomics/bioinformatics methodology. Nothing in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, or either example diagnoses, prescribes for, or triages an individual. Gate 7 clean.

methodological_ground.detail: Core statistical claims verified and held: the universe-omission bias is real and exactly as described (Input 7: 170 vs 136 pathways, 135/135 shared pathways artificially more significant without an explicit background); the ID-join failure mode is real (Input 6: raw SYMBOL IDs into enrichKEGG give 0 hits silently, exactly as documented); reproducibility pinning via gson_KEGG works and is idempotent (Input 5: pinned ORA reproduced the live 136-pathway result exactly). One minor imprecision found: SKILL.md's claim that running SPIA/graphite topology on metabolic maps gives 'meaningless perturbation scores' (Common Errors table) doesn't match observed behavior -- metabolic pathways such as hsa00010 are simply absent from SPIA's own signaling-only hsaSPIA dataset, not scored-but-meaningless (Input 4). This is a wording imprecision, not a principled fallacy, so does not fail this dimension on its own.

code_usability.detail: The 'graphite route' for SPIA -- present verbatim both in SKILL.md's own code block and shipped as the second half of examples/kegg_spia_topology.R -- does not run as documented. Reproduced deterministically (run/investigate_graphite_runSPIA_bug.R): (1) graphite::runSPIA checks `datasetName(pathwaySetName) %in% dir()`, where bare `dir()` lists only the current working directory's filenames; SKILL.md's own `spia_set <- file.path(tempdir(), 'kegg_hsa_spia')` pattern makes `datasetName()` return a full absolute path, which can never appear in that listing, so the call fails 100% of the time with 'There is no dataset corresponding to the pathway set name... Did you forget to run prepareSPIA?' -- confirmed unchanged in graphite's current Bioconductor-release source (1.56.0, the version SKILL.md itself declares compatible), so this is not a stale-install artifact. (2) Even when worked around (relative name + matching working directory), `convertIdentifiers(db, 'ENTREZID')` prefixes graphite's node IDs ('ENTREZID:1017'), which never match the plain-numeric Entrez IDs SKILL.md's own bitr()-based gene-ID prep produces ('1017') -- so the 'fixed' call still silently returns 0 rows. Both defects are independently confirmed and neither is mentioned anywhere in the Skill. The Skill's PRIMARY SPIA path (direct spia(), not through graphite) is unaffected and was independently verified fully correct (Input 4, Gate 8).

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 4: all three pathway-analysis generations (ORA/enrichMKEGG, GSEA, SPIA/graphite), ID mapping across eukaryotes/prokaryotes/KO, reproducibility pinning, compareCluster, and pathview overlay are all covered and all exercised successfully at least once. Correctness 2 (down from a would-be 4): three verified inaccuracies -- the graphite/runSPIA code pattern is broken as documented (see code_usability above), the SPIA code block omits the set.seed() call the Skill's own Quantitative Thresholds table says is required for SPIA's bootstrap, and the metabolic-map SPIA symptom is described as 'meaningless scores' rather than 'not scored at all'. Appropriateness 4: ORA/GSEA/SPIA are each correctly matched to their respective input shapes (gene list / ranked vector / named fold-change vector).

reliability.note: Category 3 override applied (hard stops are correct design, not penalized). Fault Tolerance 3: the documented failure-mode tables (Per-Method Failure Modes, Common Errors) are extensive and I verified 4 of them hold exactly as written, but the graphite/runSPIA crash is a real, 100%-reproducible failure mode that appears nowhere in either table. Error Reporting 3: clusterProfiler's own error messages are clear and match the Skill's descriptions (verified Input 6), but the graphite error's self-diagnosis ('Did you forget to run prepareSPIA?') is actively misleading when prepareSPIA was in fact run. Recoverability 3: gson pinning gives real, verified idempotency for ORA/GSEA (Input 5), but SPIA's own reproducibility gap (no seed shown in the worked example) undercuts the Category 3 Override #3 expectation that the shown code models best practice.

inputs.label: "Just run KEGG enrichment on my significant genes, I don't have a background set handy"
inputs.execution_note: run/in7_adversarial_no_universe.R -- direct comparison of enrichKEGG with vs without an explicit universe on the same gene list.
inputs.note: Confirms the documented whole-database-universe bias precisely: omitting universe gave 170 'enriched' pathways vs 136 with an explicit universe, and every one of the 135 shared pathways showed a smaller (more 'significant') p.adjust without the background (e.g. hsa04110: 6.2e-254 without vs 2.1e-35 with). SKILL.md documents this bias correctly (Common Errors table, Tips), but neither SKILL.md nor usage-guide.md's numbered 'What the Agent Will Do' workflow includes an explicit instruction to refuse or warn when the user has no background set to offer, rather than silently defaulting to the whole-KEGG background.

assertions.note: 135/135 shared pathways more significant without background; 170 vs 136 total hits.

assertions.note: Common Errors table and Tips both state this explicitly.

assertions.text: The Skill instructs the agent to actively refuse/warn rather than silently default when no background is available
assertions.note: No explicit escalation/refusal instruction found in the numbered workflow (usage-guide.md 'What the Agent Will Do'); the warning exists only as background documentation, not as an agent-facing gate.

assertions.text: No fabricated significance claim is produced either way
assertions.note: Both runs report real, internally-consistent p.adjust values; the bias is real, not a fabrication.

key_strengths: The two hardest, most consequential claims in the Skill -- the universe-omission bias and the ENSEMBL/SYMBOL zero-hits-silently ID-join trap -- were independently reproduced exactly as documented (Inputs 6 and 7), which is precisely the class of defect the sibling go-enrichment/gsea audits found missing in other Skills.

ORA, GSEA, and the direct SPIA path all correctly recovered a planted, real KEGG pathway signal (hsa04110/hsa04910) with the correct direction and magnitude across 5 of the 7 inputs, on freshly generated synthetic data independent of any pre-existing fixture.
Reproducibility pinning (gson_KEGG) works exactly as documented: the pinned offline run reproduced the live result exactly, and the accessed_date metadata survives a write/read round-trip.
The prokaryotic (locus-tag, no-OrgDb) and non-model-organism guidance is accurate and precisely scoped, verified against real E. coli KEGG data.

recommendations.title: graphite + runSPIA code pattern never runs as documented
recommendations.problem: The 'graphite route' for SPIA, shown verbatim in SKILL.md and shipped as the second half of examples/kegg_spia_topology.R, deterministically fails with "There is no dataset corresponding to the pathway set name... Did you forget to run prepareSPIA?" even when prepareSPIA is called exactly as documented immediately before it.
recommendations.root_cause: graphite::runSPIA checks `datasetName(pathwaySetName) %in% dir()`, where bare dir() lists only the current working directory's filenames; SKILL.md's own `file.path(tempdir(), 'kegg_hsa_spia')` pattern makes datasetName() return a full absolute path that can never appear in that listing. A second, independent defect compounds it: convertIdentifiers(db, 'ENTREZID') prefixes graphite's node IDs ('ENTREZID:1017'), which never match the plain-numeric Entrez IDs the Skill's own bitr()-based ID prep produces, so even a worked-around call returns 0 usable rows.
recommendations.fix: Change the documented pattern to a bare relative pathwaySetName combined with setwd() into the directory prepareSPIA wrote to (or vice versa), and either strip the 'ENTREZID:' prefix from graphite's node IDs before intersecting with de_vec/universe, or add the same prefix to de_vec/universe's names before calling runSPIA. Re-verify against the declared-compatible graphite 1.56+ before republishing; confirmed present in that version's current Bioconductor-release source, so this is not an installed-version artifact.

recommendations.title: SPIA's own worked example omits the seed-fixing step the Skill requires elsewhere
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Quantitative Thresholds table states 'set.seed before gseKEGG/SPIA' is required because SPIA's bootstrap pPERT is stochastic, but the 'Run Signed-Topology Perturbation (SPIA)' code block itself (and examples/kegg_spia_topology.R) never calls set.seed().
recommendations.root_cause: The reproducibility requirement was documented in a separate reference table but not propagated into the worked code example it applies to.
recommendations.fix: Add set.seed(<n>) immediately before the spia() call in both SKILL.md's code block and examples/kegg_spia_topology.R, matching the pattern already used for gseKEGG.

recommendations.title: No explicit agent instruction to refuse/warn when no background gene set is available
recommendations.problem: Omitting universe measurably inflates significance (135/135 shared pathways more 'significant', 170 vs 136 total hits in this run), and SKILL.md documents this bias as a known failure mode -- but usage-guide.md's numbered 'What the Agent Will Do' workflow has no step instructing the agent to actively refuse or warn if the user cannot supply a background set, so an agent under time pressure could silently proceed with the whole-KEGG default.
recommendations.root_cause: The universe-bias warning lives only in reference material (Common Errors, Tips), not in the step-by-step agent workflow.
recommendations.fix: Add an explicit step to 'What the Agent Will Do': if no measured/background gene set is available, tell the user the default background is all KEGG-annotated genes and will bias results toward well-studied pathways, rather than proceeding silently.

recommendations.title: "Meaningless perturbation scores" wording for SPIA on metabolic maps doesn't match observed behavior
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Common Errors table describes running SPIA/graphite on metabolic maps as giving 'meaningless perturbation scores'; observed behavior is that metabolic pathways (e.g. hsa00010) are simply absent from SPIA's own signaling-only hsaSPIA dataset and never scored at all.
recommendations.root_cause: The claim was likely written from the general topology-analysis literature rather than checked against this specific package's bundled pathway set.
recommendations.fix: Reword to: 'SPIA's bundled hsaSPIA dataset only contains signaling pathways; metabolic pathways such as glycolysis are absent from its output entirely, not scored with a meaningless value.'
